summary:
Turn 53 delivered the map handoff for the two most recent results, the durability call-site defect and the executor timeout protection.

State on entry. C9-durable-recorder-uses-the-instance-row is confirmed in scope (the recorder is invoked through the recovering replica's own row, and with an empty own row the call ends in a nil dereference while the instance itself lands under the owner's row), and C8-timeout-enqueues-blocked-instance is settled as a bounded no-violation protection (the executor's per-row timeout puts the blocked instance on the recovery channel after about 12.6 seconds).

Map update (accepted base version 11, three clarified objects). Behavior B2-phase1-attributes gained a branch recording the confirmed wrong-row recording when recording is enabled; Behavior B7-execute-scheduler gained an existing-protection entry for the confirmed timeout enqueue; and core_overview gained one open detail for the durability call-site defect (noting that the case where the recovering replica's row actually holds an instance at that number is still unread) plus a clause in the connection explanation stating that progress after a rejected round comes from the timeout path rather than from any rejection signal. Each object carries a map_changes entry with sources and a preserves explanation, so no requirement, binding, edge, identity or fact relation moved, and the phase-1 attribute derivation, executor scan and overview structure are unchanged.

Frontier. Nine claims are settled — seven confirmed violations or consequences (C1, C2, C3, C4, C6, C7, C9) and two bounded no-violation protections (C5, C8) — with two paused candidates holding their resume conditions and only the scope-issue bookkeeping on the superseded C1 artifact visible as administrative debt. No requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
